 Meenakshi Sengupta Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:08 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: CW Network The new Gilmore Girls documentary, Drink Coffee, Talk Fast , which premiered on November 13, is revealing some surprising details about the beloved series. Although Alexis Bledel , who played Rory Gilmore, did not participate in the documentary, her former co-stars and crew members recalled the challenges she faced while adjusting to the show's demanding filming schedule.
 Alexis Bledel's "Gilmore Girls" colleague recalls challenges she faced during filming
 Speaking about Alexis, first assistant camera Mark Strasburg shared, as per Decider , "She was just like 18 years old, and 'I'm here for 60, 70 hours a week. What am I doing with my life?' And it's pretty gruelling." Strasburg continued, "It's something you really had to want to do. There were definitely moments she knew she didn't want to be there."
 Chad Michael Murray, who portrayed Rory's classmate Tristan DuGray, also recalled how quiet Bledel was on set. He noted that she was relatively unfamiliar with the entertainment industry at the time. With countless lines to memorize and deliver quickly, the young actor had a lot to manage.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Unlike many other television shows, which typically had scripts of 45 to 50 pages, Gilmore Girls scripts reportedly stretched to 80 or 90 pages. The show's creator, Amy Sherman-Palladino, also expected the cast to be "word perfect" with their dialogue.
 Director Jamie Babbit shared another memory of Bledel's exhaustion. "The only time in my 30-year career of directing that I've had an actor fall asleep on camera in the middle of a scene was Alexis Bledel," she said. Babbit added, "When Alexis got the role, I don't think she really realized that it was going to be six years of her life. I think she was pretty relieved to finally have a life."
 Over its seven-season run, Gilmore Girls aired 153 episodes between October 5, 2000, and May 15, 2007. The new documentary , directed by Meghna Balakumar and Kevin Konrad Hanna, is available to stream on Apple TV.
